verdict.rationale: Flagsmith documents a self-hosted Edge Proxy that runs an instance of the Flagsmith Engine in your own infrastructure, which is a first-party relay layer for flag evaluation. However, the docs describe it as running close to your servers and being reached from server-side SDKs, not close to end users, and nothing shows CDN-worker evaluation. The community remark about primarily server-side evaluation does not concretely contradict the Edge Proxy, so it creates no dispute. Missing for 10: CDN/edge-worker evaluation support (e.g., Cloudflare Workers or similar), evidence of deployment close to end users rather than servers, client-side SDK use of the relay, and independent or hands-on corroboration of Edge Proxy performance.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can evaluate flags at the edge (CDN workers or an edge/relay layer) close to users

citations.quote: The Flagsmith Edge Proxy is a service that you host yourself, that allows you to run an instance of the Flagsmith Engine close to your servers.
Run the Edge Proxy within in your own infrastructure and connect to it from your server-side SDKs
